scenery.label: Centrosome
sizes: What it is

The cell's centre for organising its microtubules: two centrioles, short barrels at right angles, in a cloud of protein. In an animal cell the Golgi gathers round it, beside the nucleus. A plant cell has none.
Drawn
Two barrels of nine rods, each 0.9 µm long and 0.38 µm across, enlarged, between the nucleus and the Golgi: the picture's choice. Nothing in the engine stands behind it.

chromatin: One closed thread 3.3 nm thick and 6.8 µm long, in the part of the cell kept below the cut. Its 543 kbp would make about 185 µm of DNA 2 nm thick, at 0.34 nm a base pair (textbook figures): the thread shows about 4% of that length. Its width, its length and how it winds are the picture's choice.
ribosomes: Drawn

22, standing for the 300 of the 500 the species' file gives that are in the part of the cell kept below the cut: each enlarged 2.4 times, as the membrane's proteins are here, so fewer are drawn, as many as fill the same share of the cell. Each as its two subunits, each the ellipsoid of the same spread as its atoms: the ribosome of Escherichia coli, as the viewer measured it from the Protein Data Bank's entry 7K00, the large subunit 20.6 by 18 by 14.3 nm across and the small one 23.5 by 15.2 by 10 nm, the whole 26.1 by 21.1 by 17.3 nm. No structure of Syn3A's own ribosome is among its file's sources: it is drawn at E. coli's measure. Gilbert and others 2021 took a ribosome to be about 20 nm across in their model of the cell, and found the ribosomes in their tomograms with a structure of E. coli's ribosome (the entry 5MDZ) as the template.

chromatin: A fine line, in a slab 10 nm deep under the cut, as an electron tomogram shows a cell: 9.6 µm of the 185 µm its 543 kbp would make as DNA, at 0.34 nm a base pair, 2 nm across (textbook figures). That is the share the slab holds of the region the chromosome fills in the middle of the cell; drawn whole, it would cover most of the cut face. Where that region lies and how the line winds are the picture's choice.

63 of them, each 5.6 µm across: the ones that lie in the part of the cell that is kept. That each is a little flatter than it is wide is the picture's choice.
Colour
Green, as a chloroplast is. It is the one piece of scenery with a colour of its own, and says nothing of a status: where colour shows status it is neutral like the rest.

A wedge of it is cut away, as of a globe, to show the two membranes of its envelope, the chromatin and the nucleolus.
